title: Travel
text:
Niagara Falls
FIELD NOTES / A DIFFERENT PACE
Some places make it easier to slow down and pay attention. Here, the movement of the water and the scale of the landscape are a reminder to look beyond the frame of a photograph.
I’m interested in the small details that make a place feel different: how people move through it, where they gather, and what they stop to notice.

title: What a chart can tell me
text: A chart makes some patterns easier to see, but it also reflects a series of choices. Which observations belong in the plot? What belongs on each axis? Which differences deserve attention?

title: What a chart can tell me
text:
One choice that matters
In a comparison of income and life expectancy, a logarithmic income axis changes the spacing of the values. That can help reveal patterns that are difficult to see when a few large values stretch the scale.

title: What a chart can tell me
section: What I still need to ask
text:
What I still need to ask
A visible association does not explain why the pattern exists. Before moving from description to explanation, I need to think about the research question, the data, and possible alternative explanations.
My next step is to describe the plot in one careful sentence, then write down a question it cannot answer.

title: Areas of Interest and Explorations
text:
Sitting at the intersection of quantitative political analysis and critical gender theory, my research examines how race, gender, and social dynamics shape power structures and political outcomes. By anchoring my research methodology in intersectional frameworks, I analyze the foundations underlying political behaviors, societal tendencies, representation and institutional power.

Intersectional Political Behaviors: How do race and gender shape who holds power, who participates in political discourse, and who is excluded from representation.
Critical Systems & Power Structures: How do institutions and social norms shape policy outcomes, and work to challenge or uphold structural system of gender and radicalized inequality.
Data and communication: How quantitative data and empirical methods showcase structural systems of power, labor and inequality?

title: Academic interests & research
text:
A project I’m developing

Comparing life expectancy across countries
COURSE PROJECT · IN PROGRESS
Question. How does life expectancy vary with income across countries in a given year?
Approach. Use R to explore the historical Gapminder data and make a clearly labeled visualization.
What I’m learning. Choosing the year, scale, and unit of analysis changes what readers can see. An association in a plot is a starting point for questions, not evidence of a causal effect.
Read a reflection on this project

title: Areas of Interest and Explorations
text:
Research in the Works:
CURRENT PROJECTS · IN PROGRESS

Computational Analysis of Psychoanalytic Archetypes: The Virgin / Whore Dichotomy:
Through utilizing quantitative methodology and discourse to support my research examines how cultural and psychoanalytical archetypes shape societal standards regarding gender. This project, which will serve as both a Women’s & Gender Studies capstone project, along with a future publication piece, quantifies the Virgin / Whore binary through a close examination of the Virgin Mary’s symbolic representation, iconography, and discourse, analyzing and outlining how social dichotomies shape deeply historical, hierarchical, gendered dynamics.


Empirical Examination of Federal Poilicy and Food Insecurity on Native American Tribal Lands:
Conducting a computational analysis in order to uncover the structural and governmental catalysts of food insecurity across Native American populations. Collecting data from prior academia along with collecting, extracting, examining and analyzing data from local and national datasets, this project will provide an comprehensive and well rounded answer to the following question: Why are there high rates of food insecurity on tribal lands?

text:
Pending Publications:
CURRENT PUBLICATIONS · IN PROGRESS

One Nation Under God: A Statistical Analysis of Religiosity, Patriotism, and Racial Bias in the United States
Research Question. Are White Christian individuals more likely to harbor racist resentment in comparison to their non-Christian counterparts?
Hypothesis. We hypothesize that White Christians will harbor more racial resentment compared to their White non-Christian counterparts. Additionally, we hypothesize that, when controlling for patriotism, White Christians with higher levels of patriotism are even more likely to harbor feelings of resentment toward different racial groups.
Approach. Use R Studio to analyze data from the 2024 American National Elections Survey to create advanced regressions, models, and visulizations

title: Travel
text:
London, United Kingdom
FIELD NOTES
Every single winter break I travel to London to visit my father, who is based in Fullham Brodway. Each time I discover something new about the history and culture of this historic and diverse city. Visting London is one of my favorite parts of my winter break, and it is something I look forward to each and every year.

title: Travel
text:
Venice, Italy
FIELD NOTES
Each summer, my mother, sisters and I travel to a new country, and these past two summers we have explored various locations in Europe with my Grandmother. These experiences are truly some of my favorite, as I adore watching my grandmother experience traveling to new countries and experiences the beauty, history and diversty of European countries that I have taken for granted in my previous visits.
